question: If cos x = - (3)/(5) and x lies in the third quadrant, then the value of the sin x is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In the **third quadrant**, the **sine** function is always negative.

Given **cos x = −3/5**, we identify the **3-4-5 Pythagorean triplet** where base = 3 and hypotenuse = 5.

The **perpendicular** is 4, so the magnitude of **sin x** is 4/5.

Since **x** is in the **third quadrant**, sin x must be negative.

**∴ The correct answer is −4/5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** cos x = −3/5 and **x** lies in the **third quadrant** (180° [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/40f35c8d54f1723913349df8d722376b583360a77765b9f984e286dde064609e.png] 

⇒ sin²x = 1 − cos²x

⇒ sin²x = 1 − (−3/5)²

⇒ sin²x = 1 − 9/25

⇒ sin²x = 16/25

⇒ sin x = ± √(16/25) = ± 4/5

Since **x** lies in the **third quadrant**, the **sine** value is negative (sin x [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

ASTC Rule

This rule determines the sign of trigonometric ratios: **All** positive in Q1, **Sine** in Q2, **Tangent** in Q3, and **Cosine** in Q4.

Pythagorean Identity

For any angle x, the identity **sin²x + cos²x = 1** always holds true, derived from the Pythagorean theorem.

Trigonometric Ratios

In a right-angled triangle, **sin θ = Perpendicular/Hypotenuse** and **cos θ = Base/Hypotenuse**.
